subject.title: Feature: config option to route gateway lifecycle warnings to a dedicated channel

question: Should OpenClaw add a general `messages` internal-warning router, and if so what categories and defaults should it support?
rationale: The requested fix creates new config and delivery semantics across shared message dispatch, existing suppression knobs, cron failure destinations, and channel behavior; code inspection cannot choose that product contract safely.

options.title: Approve a canonical router
options.body: Add one default-compatible routing policy for lifecycle, tool-error, and system notices, with docs and tests proving current default visibility plus explicit operator opt-in.

options.title: Narrow to suppression only
options.body: Keep improving `messages.suppressToolErrors` and cron-specific destinations without adding a general ops-channel target, reducing config growth but leaving no dedicated warning channel.

options.title: Reject new config surface
options.body: Keep current behavior and close the routing request as not planned, accepting continued active-channel warning noise for operators.

recommendation.title: Approve a canonical router
recommendation.body: Add one default-compatible routing policy for lifecycle, tool-error, and system notices, with docs and tests proving current default visibility plus explicit operator opt-in.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent current-main work carried the central reply/config paths, and this choice is primarily about product/config direction rather than one narrow implementation bug.
